title: OpenAI drops another batch of mathematical breakthroughs
key_facts: OpenAI released a batch of 722 manuscripts covering 372 'result families' that group related papers, produced by an unreleased frontier model.
AGMAI, a newly formed independent advisory group of leading mathematicians, says the release includes solutions to 'hundreds' of open questions.
In September OpenAI said the model had 'resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics'.
OpenAI says the average result used about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking time.
The papers are published in a GitHub repository; OpenAI says it is exploring community-hosted alternatives that meet AGMAI's guidelines.
AGMAI's late-September recommendations urged labs to release results promptly through academic channels and disclose the model, prompts and compute, and not to use results as marketing.
The Verge says mathematicians still have to assess the results and that the speed of AI labs' entry into mathematics has caused fierce debate over ethics and credit.
quote_evidence: According to AGMAI, ... the release includes solutions to “hundreds” of open questions.
OpenAI claims the “average result” used the equivalent of three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking.
The full impact of the results will likely take some time to be felt as mathematicians assess and digest them.
why_it_matters_hint: Mathematicians have yet to check hundreds of AI-produced results, and the release is the first test of the new advisory group's disclosure guidelines.
notes: Follow-up of the 6 Oct 2026 edition's AI math item; today's new fact is the batch release of 722 manuscripts. Results are OpenAI's claims, not yet independently checked.
